source: EPCCG: Trait Edition, Revision 2 (with budget from Traits v2; rules from PHC Core Rules v1.0)

rules.note: Trait bonuses add to rolls only; they never unlock perks, skill unlocks or classes.
rules.budget_note: Design budget: upside minus downside is about +3 SP; +1 on a roll costs 2 SP. Per-trait prices are not recorded in the source docs, so cost is null.
rules.music_shared: All three share these rules. You start with a Musek Blestor, and the player picks a real song for the character's Favourite Song field. Starting the song costs 2 AP, or it starts on its own when you kill, revive an ally, or land a big heal or shield; while it plays, it replaces the area or combat music. The bonus fades after 2 area changes without the song; the penalty starts after 4.

items.name: Mind Without Fog
items.flavour: You were raised in a Lumeri cloister, or by priests of some other faith. Whatever you believe now, your mind is still water. Nobody has ever managed to stir it.
upsides: Still Water: gain 2 Core points at creation, to raise any Core above what your skills need. Heart Debuffs never affect you.
downsides: Unmoving: gear bonuses to Attributes and Skills don't work on you, and your Karma can never change.
notes: Mechanical note: 'Karma can never change' locks Karma at its starting value.
items.narrator_hook: every faction wants to convert the one recruit who can't be converted.
items.text:
You were raised in a Lumeri cloister, or by priests of some other faith. Whatever you believe now, your mind is still water. Nobody has ever managed to stir it.

− Unmoving: gear bonuses to Attributes and Skills don't work on you, and your Karma can never change.

items.name: The Brightest Light
items.flavour: Burn it down, all of it. The brightest light burns out the fastest, and you've never cared how long you last.
upsides: Blaze: each kill this combat gives +10% damage, up to +50%.
downsides: Burnout: weapons wear twice as fast in your hands, and when the fighting stops you crash: −2 on every roll until you rest.
items.narrator_hook: the fight that should never have started, right before the one nobody can avoid.

items.name: Southern Fist
items.flavour: You trained with the southern sects, where martial arts and magic were never separated. Your fists are weapons. Anything else in your hands is a clumsy stick.
upsides: These Hands: while fighting with nothing but gloves, +1 AP per turn and +20% Physical Damage.
downsides: Not That: every attack with any other weapon, guns included, costs +1 AP.
items.narrator_hook: armoured targets, fights across a canyon, and zones where only gunfire reaches.

items.name: Forlorn Hope
items.flavour: The Hellraiser storm units go in first and come back last, if they come back at all. You volunteered, and you'd volunteer again.
upsides: Charge: +2 AP on any turn you end closer to an enemy than you started.
downsides: No Way Back: no armour above Class I, and you can never take the Retreat or Disengage action.
items.narrator_hook: the mission where the smart move is to fall back.

items.name: Grenadier's Arm
items.flavour: In the mess halls they arm-wrestle. In the field you throw: grenades, crates, Orks, the occasional squadmate.
upsides: Long Throw: +2 throwing range. You can throw anything under your carry weight, allies and enemies included; damage scales with its weight.
downsides: Strained Arm: thrown weapons cost +1 AP.
items.narrator_hook: the squadmate who needs to be on the other side of the gap right now.

items.name: Glass Runner
items.flavour: You were born on a low-gravity mining moon, and your bones never set right in real gravity. So you learned to move before anything could break them.
upsides: Runner: +5 Initiative, and your first move each combat costs 1 AP less.
downsides: Glass: +50% limb damage taken. A broken leg halves your Movement until it's set.
items.narrator_hook: called shots to the legs.

items.name: Blade Recluse
items.flavour: While your cohort at the academy drank and courted, you trained alone with one blade. Now the world is ending, and suddenly everyone wants to know you.
upsides: One Blade: weapon mastery levels 25% faster. Name one weapon: it can't be disarmed and gets one extra mod slot.
downsides: Rusty Manners: −1 Charisma, Implication and Authority. If anyone asks about your weapon, you tell them, at length.
items.narrator_hook: the negotiation where someone compliments the sword.

items.flavour: Four-eyes, bookworm, glass-jaw. You've been called a lot of names, most of them accurate, but they didn't have to say it out loud.

downsides: Glasses Off: without them, −4 Proficiency and Ingenuity.
items.narrator_hook: enemies can aim for the glasses; rain, smoke and fistfights knock them off.

downsides: Bare Face: unmasked, −3 Composure and Authority.
Two Faces: people who met you masked don't recognise you unmasked, and the other way round.

items.name: Machine-Faced
items.flavour: You bought a new face at a back-alley clinic in Central City. It was a robot clinic. Nobody told the surgeon you weren't a robot.
upsides: Blank Face: every Composure check in dialogue succeeds. Robots and machines treat you as one of their own.
downsides: Uncanny: you can't use Implication or Charisma in dialogue (their combat perks still work), and children and animals panic around you.
items.narrator_hook: the scene that needs a warm human face.

items.flavour: Central City's streets don't move aside for anyone, and neither do you. Your limp has been there since the old injury; you just walk through it.
upsides: I'm Walking Here: against anyone who blocks your path or interrupts you, +2 Intimidation and Authority. You can't be moved by Shove.
downsides: Old Injury: −0.5 Movement, −2 Reaction Speed.
items.narrator_hook: crowds, queues, and anyone who wants you to wait.

items.name: Drill Echo
items.flavour: Ten years ago you passed the academy's endurance drill with the best time in your cohort. The announcer's voice never stopped counting in your head.
upsides: Best Time: the Sprint action costs 1 AP less, and running, climbing and endurance checks can't roll below 10.
downsides: The Count: whenever you concentrate (drawing a Sigil, a Brain Power or Rumination check), roll a d6. On a 1 the count starts again, and you lose the action.
items.narrator_hook: quiet, high-stakes thinking.

items.name: The Old Blood
items.flavour: You distrust anything unusual. You're conservative, and you don't want anything to change. Your own blood first, and only.
upsides: Bloodline: +2 Rumination and Guts. Among people of your own race and homeworld, +2 Authority.
downsides: Prejudice: with people of any other race, +2 Intimidation but −2 Charisma, Authority and Lore Master. Heals and Blessings from them work at half power on you, and you buy from them at +20% and sell to them at −20%.
items.narrator_hook: the squadmate, quest-giver or medic who isn't your kind, on the day your life depends on them.

items.name: Holo-Drama Addict
items.flavour: Three days without food, or three days without a holo-drama? You'd live on water.
upsides: Dramatic Timing: once per scene, describe your action as a scene from a holo-drama. If the Narrator buys the drama, roll with +3.
downsides: Leading Role: anything unglamorous (crawling through sewage, hiding in a bin) takes a Visualization check first: you have to picture it as a scene worth filming. On a fail you refuse, or do it at −3.

downsides: Paper: −1 Durability, Pain Threshold and Sensory. With both Oil traits, this penalty applies once.
items.narrator_hook: gang tags, forged paintings, propaganda posters, a killer's "art."

items.name: Lunarshine
items.flavour: Part gentleman, part lush. A glass of Mandestra vintage, or the whole jug of lowland rotgut?
upsides: Tipsy (1 drink): +1 Camaraderie, Lore Master and Authority.
Drunk (3 drinks): a further +1 to those, plus Intimidation, Guts and Durability.
downsides: Wasted (5 drinks): −2 Reaction Speed, Dexterity, Proficiency, Vigilant, Analysis and Visualization.

The Slope: drinks wear off at the end of each scene. When a scene ends with you Drunk, make a Will Power check (target 12 + drinks today); on a fail you keep drinking, one step closer to Wasted. A day with no drink at all gives you the shakes: −1 Camaraderie, Authority and Composure.
items.narrator_hook: the bar scene, the dry mission, the open bottle in the evidence room.

items.name: Heavyworlder
items.flavour: Born on a high-gravity world. Your mother has never forgiven you, the bullies at school never forgot you, and doorframes still don't fit you.
upsides: Dense: you count as one size larger. You can't be Shoved, your carry weight doubles, you wield heavy weapons one-handed, and you get +2 Intimidation.
downsides: Too Big: −3 Athletics and −0.5 Movement. Attacks against you get +2 to hit. You can't hide in light, you eat double rations, and vents, crawlspaces, small doors, lifts and light vehicles can't take you.
items.narrator_hook: stealth missions, tight corridors, and the rope bridge.

items.name: Ghost Soldier

downsides: The War Never Ended: resting in a settlement takes a Vigilant check, or you spend the night watching the doors and get no benefit. When your stealth is broken, you lose 2 AP on your next turn. −1 Eloquence, Charisma, Implication and Composure.

downsides: My Way: leaving Lawful costs double Karma, and every unlawful act you commit costs double Karma too.

+ Little Friend: start with a drone: 30 HP, 3 AP of its own, scouts or carries 5 kg. Proficiency repairs it.
− Tethered: if the drone is destroyed, you take a Heart Debuff until you rebuild it, which takes a rest and materials.

effects.note: drone scouts or carries 5 kg; Proficiency repairs it

items.name: Augmented
items.flavour: Part of you came out of a catalogue.
upsides: Chrome: pick one augment at creation. Arm: +20% Physical Damage. Eye: +2 Vision Range and sight in darkness. Legs: +1 Movement and jumps of up to 2 tiles.
downsides: Maintenance: after each rest, make a Proficiency check; on a fail, the augment doesn't work the next day. EMP disables it for 2 turns.
items.narrator_hook: the long mission far from a workshop.

items.name: True Believer
items.flavour: Holy Father Nerukhan, or some other saint, has never once let you down. You've never once let them down either.
upsides: Unshaken: Blessing cooldowns are 1 turn shorter. Once per session, your prayer is answered: the Narrator grants a small miracle.
downsides: Rites: keep your church's daily rites (dawn prayer, fasting days). Each day you can't, −1 Faith and Will Power until you make amends.
items.narrator_hook: the mission that makes the rites impossible.

items.name: Heaven's Faithful
items.flavour: The Department fights Heaven. You pray to it. If they ever find out, they'll shoot you.
upsides: Communion: once per scene, ask your twin soul in the upper realm one question. The Narrator answers truthfully, but in riddles. +2 Outburst Range.
downsides: Treason: if the Department learns your faith, you're hunted. Each time you fight upper-realm beings, make a Faith check or hesitate and lose 2 AP.
items.narrator_hook: the upper-realm being who calls you by name.

items.name: Occultist
items.flavour: The Institute of Forgotten Knowledge lent you one book. You never gave it back.
upsides: Forbidden Text: start with a grimoire. Once per session, learn any supernatural creature's weakness. Out of combat, you can spend 10 minutes warding an area against the supernatural.
downsides: Overdue: the Institute wants its book back. The book talks too: once per session, the Narrator whispers you one false line through it.
items.narrator_hook: Mother Lovelace's collectors.

items.name: Crawler-Blooded
items.flavour: Your grandmother crossed the line at Daggerfall. Her blood still shows under your skin.
upsides: Chitin: 30% less limb damage taken. You can climb walls at half Movement, and Crawlers never attack you first.
downsides: Marked: humans who see your blood start hostile. Lumeri Blessings burn you for 10 damage before they take effect.
items.narrator_hook: Daggerfall's survivors, on both sides.

items.name: Old Timer
items.flavour: You were already old when Daggerfall happened.
upsides: Seen It All: start each session with 1 extra Echo (2). Once per session, declare you've seen this before: one Rumination, Lore Master or Analysis check succeeds automatically.
downsides: Old Bones: −0.5 Movement and −10% max HP. Without a full night's rest, −2 on every Body skill the next day.
items.narrator_hook: the forced march.

items.name: Pacifist
items.flavour: You won't kill. Not even them.
upsides: Sanctuary: while you haven't attacked this combat, enemies get −2 to hit you. Every attack you make can be nonlethal, and enemies you defeat that way surrender to a talk at +3. Mercy earns you double Karma.
downsides: The Vow: if you kill, lose all your Echo and take a Heart Debuff for the rest of the session.
items.narrator_hook: the enemy who will never stop unless someone stops them for good.

items.name: Moon Hunter
items.flavour: You tracked game across three moons before you ever tracked a man.
upsides: Tracker: follow any trail less than a day old. Your first attack on a creature you tracked this scene does +30% damage.
downsides: Wild Born: in cities, −2 Charisma, Eloquence and Authority.
items.narrator_hook: the hunt that leads into Central City.

items.name: Beast Handler
items.flavour: It came to you half-starved. Now it would die for you, and nearly has.
upsides: Companion: a trained beast fights at your side: 60 HP, 4 AP of its own, bite and grapple. It obeys your Empathy checks.
downsides: Bond: if it dies, you take a Heart Debuff for the rest of the campaign arc. It can't enter most buildings in Central City.
items.narrator_hook: the place where beasts aren't allowed.

items.name: Ace Pilot
items.flavour: Give you anything with an engine and you'll find out what it can really do.
upsides: Born Behind the Stick: you can drive or pilot anything with an engine. Vehicles you drive get +1 Movement, and use your Dodge.
downsides: Grounded: after a full day on foot, −0.5 Movement and −1 Reaction Speed until you're back in a seat.
items.narrator_hook: the mission where everything with an engine is gone.
